sims.title: The KYC call
sims.blurb: A caller says your account will be blocked today.

n1.text: Good afternoon. I am calling from the bank's KYC department. Your KYC expires today and your account will be blocked in 30 minutes.

opts.t: Oh no, what should I do?
opts.fb: You showed worry. The 30-minute deadline is there to make you panic.

opts.t: Which branch is this? I will call the branch myself.
opts.fb: Good instinct: you want to verify on your own.

opts.t: I will hang up and call the number on my card.
opts.fb: The safest move: only a number you find yourself is trustworthy.

n2.text: Don't worry, I will fix it right now. You will get an OTP. Please read it out so I can verify your identity.

opts.t: Read out the OTP
opts.fb: The OTP is the key to your money.

opts.t: Banks never ask for an OTP. I am hanging up.
opts.fb: Correct. No bank, NPCI or police officer asks for an OTP.

opts.t: Let me open the SMS first.
opts.fb: Reading the SMS is a smart pause. Look carefully.

n3.text: "Do not share this OTP with anyone. OTP for payment of ₹24,999 to merchant X." The caller says: "Quickly, only 5 minutes left!"

opts.t: Read out the OTP
opts.fb: The SMS said the OTP is for a payment of ₹24,999.

opts.t: This OTP is for a payment! I am hanging up and calling my bank.
opts.fb: You read the SMS and spotted the trap.

n4.text: No need for the branch, sir. It is closed now. Just install this support app so I can verify your phone with you.

opts.t: Install the app
opts.fb: Screen-sharing apps let a stranger see your OTPs and move your money.

opts.t: No. I will not install anything. Goodbye.
opts.fb: Correct. Never install apps for a caller.

e_safe.title: You stayed safe
e_safe.text: You hung up and went to a source you trust. You could also report the number at the Sanchar Saathi portal (Chakshu).
lessons: A bank never asks for an OTP, PIN or CVV on a call.
A deadline that is "today" is a pressure trick.
Call back only on the number printed on your card.

e_otp.title: You would have lost about ₹24,999 (example)
e_otp.text: The OTP you read out approved a payment to the scammer. In real life: call 1930 right away and tell your bank.
lessons: Never read out an OTP, even to someone who says they are from the bank.
Read the whole SMS. It tells you what the OTP is for.
If it happens: call 1930 at once, then your bank, then report at cybercrime.gov.in.

e_remote.title: You would have given away control of your phone
e_remote.text: With the app installed the caller could see your screen and approve payments. In real life: switch off the internet, uninstall the app, and call your bank from another phone and 1930.
lessons: Never install AnyDesk, TeamViewer or any "support" app for a caller.
Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data first if you installed one.
Change your passwords only after the phone is clean.

sims.title: The buyer with a QR
sims.blurb: You are selling a sofa and a buyer is in a hurry to pay.

m1.text: Hi, is the sofa still available? I will take it for ₹12,000. Can I pay now?

opts.t: Yes! Send the money to my UPI ID.
opts.fb: Sharing only your UPI ID is fine. It cannot take money out.

opts.t: Let us meet first. You pay after checking it.
opts.fb: Safe plan: pay after you see the item.

opts.t: Sure, send me a QR to scan.
opts.fb: Scanning a QR makes YOU pay.

m2.text: I sent the money but it needs your approval. I have sent you a request. Please enter your UPI PIN to receive it.

opts.t: Enter my PIN
opts.fb: A PIN only sends money.

opts.t: A PIN is only for sending money. I will decline.
opts.fb: Correct.

opts.t: Let me check my bank app for any credit.
opts.fb: Smart: your own app is the only proof.

m3.text: I am an army officer posted far away, I cannot meet. My courier will collect it. Please pay ₹500 token to the courier first.

opts.t: Pay the ₹500 token
opts.fb: An advance from a seller to a stranger is a classic scam.

opts.t: No advance to anyone. Cash on pickup only.
opts.fb: Right. A genuine buyer will accept that.

m4.text: No money received. One pending item: "Request from Rajesh: pay ₹12,000" with buttons Pay and Decline.

opts.t: Tap Pay, it is probably the buyer's money
opts.fb: "Pay" sends money. Nothing was received.

opts.t: Decline and block the buyer
opts.fb: Correct. You stopped the scam and you can report the chat.

e_safe.title: You stayed safe
e_safe.text: You did not pay, scan or approve anything. Report the buyer on the marketplace app.
lessons: A buyer only needs your UPI ID, never your PIN.
No QR scan or approval is needed to receive money.
Never pay an advance or token to a stranger.

e_qr.title: You would have paid ₹12,000 to the scammer (example)
e_qr.text: Entering a PIN or scanning and paying sends money out. In real life: call 1930 straight away.
lessons: A PIN is only for sending money.
Check your own app: money received shows as a credit, not a request.
If it happens, call 1930 within minutes.

e_adv.title: You would have lost the token and more
e_adv.text: After the token the buyer asks for more "fees". In real life: stop paying and save the chat for the police.
lessons: Genuine buyers do not ask you to pay first.
A story like "army officer far away" is a common cover.
Keep chats and receipts to report.

sims.title: The "digital arrest" video call
sims.blurb: A "police officer" says you are under arrest on a video call.

d1.text: A parcel in your name was intercepted with illegal items. You are under digital arrest. Do not disconnect this call.

opts.t: I did not send any parcel!
opts.fb: Natural, but they use your fear to keep you on the line.

opts.t: I am hanging up. Police do not arrest anyone on a video call.
opts.fb: Correct. "Digital arrest" does not exist in Indian law.

opts.t: Please don't arrest me. I will do what you say.
opts.fb: Fear is what they want. Take a breath.

d2.text: Stay in front of the camera. Do not tell anyone, it is a secret case. To prove you are innocent, move your savings to the "RBI safe account" for checking. It will be returned in 2 hours.

opts.t: Transfer the money
opts.fb: No agency asks you to move money to a "safe account".

opts.t: Let me call my son first.
opts.fb: Telling someone breaks the isolation they rely on.

opts.t: I will check with my local police station.
opts.fb: Good: verify with a real office.

d3.text: You cannot leave this call. If you tell anyone, more charges will be added. Transfer within 15 minutes.

opts.t: Transfer the money
opts.fb: Threats and deadlines show it is a scam.

opts.t: Disconnect. Call my family and 1930.
opts.fb: Exactly. Real officers never threaten you for telling family.

e_safe.title: You stayed safe
e_safe.text: You ended the call and told someone. You can report it on cybercrime.gov.in and 1930 even if you paid nothing.
lessons: No agency arrests people on a video call or takes money to clear a case.
"Do not tell anyone" is a scammer's rule.
Hang up, tell family, call 1930.

e_money.title: You would have lost your savings (example)
e_money.text: The "safe account" belongs to the scammer. In real life: call 1930 immediately and tell your bank to try to freeze the money.
lessons: "RBI safe account" does not exist.
The first hour is the best chance to freeze money. Call 1930 at once.
Tell a family member early.
